fixes: Make the folded shirt and laundry states visually unmistakable: show folded count, completed stack, and current shirt highlight so progress is not ambiguous on phone.
Raise visual distinctiveness: add fabric texture, stitching, subtle wear, richer lighting, and more characterful props so the scene is not a clean generic 3D mockup.
Increase visible tactile feedback for every interaction: add cloth deformation, coin/spill particles, foam, lint bits, or stronger contact shadows so actions feel physically satisfying.

evidence.C1: Visible frame shows calm warm palette, soft lighting, and good material craft on the shirt and detergent bottle; description claims 29 sounds + loops + spatial placement, but only one mid-activity frame is provided so the full sensory payoff (rain, hum, tumbling) cannot be verified.
evidence.C2: Description covers changer, coin slot drag, detergent drawer, lint trap peel, pegs, smoothing drag, and folding in thirds with gesture-named hints ('Now the right side: tap or swipe it in.'); each station has its own matched gesture.
evidence.C3: Coherent art direction visible: green grid cutting mat, 'lavanda' detergent label, warm HUD with bilas logo, tiled floor, clearcoat machines; readable 3D objects and HUD matches the place, but the overall look reads as pleasant generic cozy-game rather than a distinctive designer-screenshot identity.
evidence.C4: 'This load' card shows per-shirt state words (dry/dry/dry/dry), bottom bar highlights Fold, hint names the gesture, and progress is always visible; one clear next-step at all times with obvious navigation.

fixes: Push the visual identity past 'cozy generic' — the green mat, detergent label and warm HUD are coherent but not distinctive; introduce a stronger signature (e.g., a more memorable material/lighting motif or a unique prop silhouette) so a designer would actually screenshot it.

Make the ASMR payoff legible in the idle/mid-activity frame — the current screenshot is calm but visually quiet; add a visible ambient cue (rain beads on glass, drum swirl, steam wisp, or a peg swinging) so the scene visibly invites lingering rather than reading as a static fold task.

Verify the ghost-fingertip drag cue actually fires for the fold gestures on phone — the description claims it demos smoothing and folds, but the screenshot only shows a text hint; ensure the in-scene gesture demo is visible and timed so first-time phone users can complete the fold without confusion.

Recompose the phone fold view: ~40% of the 390px frame is empty tile floor and the lavanda jug is clipped/tilted at the left edge; lower the camera target or add floor/prop interest so the framing looks deliberate (C3/C1).

Add a visual target highlight for fold gestures (glint or outline on the exact sleeve/hem being folded) so 'tap or swipe it in' is unambiguous at a glance, pushing onboarding from hint-following to self-evident (C4/C1).
